日文.首段: 阪神155形電車（はんしん155がたでんしゃ）は、かつて阪神電気鉄道が保有していた鉄道車両で、新製の車体に流用の台車及び電装品を組み合わせた事業用の電動貨車である。本項では本形式のほか、同時期に保線作業の近代化に対応して製造された製造された事業用貨車の101形・161形についても併せて紹介する。

章节.155形:
神戸高速鉄道への乗り入れ実施に伴い、1969年8月に武庫川車両工業で製造された大型高性能救援車である。石屋川車庫に常備されていた。
車体は全長18.7m、全幅2.76mの大型車体で、先に登場した151形各形式と同じ赤茶色に塗られていた。切妻両運転台の前面には2枚の正面窓と頭部中央にヘッドライト2灯、左右には標識灯を取り付けた。1.3m幅の大きな開き戸とデッキ、パワーゲートを設け、重量物の積み下ろしを可能とした。側面には窓のない2m幅の両開き扉を2箇所、側窓はスライド式のアルミサッシ窓を片側4箇所に設けている。窓のない部分には棚やフックなどを設けて救援用の資材を搭載している。
台車及び電装品は3011形の流用品で、3561形3568の機器換装時に発生した東芝製機器を搭載、台車はTT-6を履き、モーターは出力60kWのSE-516を4個搭載し、制御器はPE-15C-Hを装備した。連結器は設置されていないが、設置可能な構造になっていた。
章节.101形: 1962年に武庫川車両工業で製造されたレール運搬車である。外観は台車の上にレール吊り上げ用のチェーンブロックと連結棒を取り付けただけのトロッコなどとよく似たものである。常時は今津駅近くの側線に留置され、出動時は151形各形式に連結されて牽引された。そのため、連結器は151形の簡易連結器の受けに対応したピンリンク式の簡易型連結器を取り付けたほか、ブレーキ装置は自動直通ブレーキのAMMを搭載した。
章节.161形: 砕石運搬用として、1965年12月に日立製作所で製造されたホッパ車である。積載荷重は25t、国鉄の同系車であるホキ800形と同一の形態で塗色も同じ黒一色であるが、バンドン式密着連結器や電車スタイルの尾灯を取り付けたところが私鉄の所有車の特徴である。101形同様常時は今津駅近くの側線に留置され、出動時はモーターカーに牽引された。ただ、151形各形式とも連結可能で、154と連結された写真が残っている。1988年12月廃車。
章节.変遷:
155形の登場時に想定されていたような事態は幸いにして発生せず、工場入出場時に石屋川車庫と尼崎車庫の間を往復するほかに動く機会はなかった。101形や161形は保線工事に出動したが、夜間の出動のため、昼間動く姿を見ることはまれであった。1971年には101が搭載する手動チェーンブロックを電動ホイストに換装している。
時代の変化に伴い、工事用の貨車を機械扱いする事業者が増加していった。阪神においても例外ではなく、1982年に101が新型レール運搬車に置き換えられて廃車され、1988年には161がダンプトロリーに代替されて廃車された。代替車はどちらも保線用の機械扱いで無車籍である。
後に155のパンタグラフは下枠交差式のものに取り替えられ、旧型救援車の153の代替車である110の登場後も石屋川車庫で待機し続けたが、実際、地下線内で事故が発生した場合には電車で近づきがたいことから、自動車で出動して事故現場近くの駅で資材を搬入して復旧作業を行うといった方法がとられるようになった。このため余剰となった155は1992年7月24日付で廃車された。

中文.首段: 阪神155型电力动车组（はんしん155がたでんしゃ）是阪神电气铁道过去保有的铁道车辆，是将新造车体与流用的转向架及电气设备组合而成的业务用电动货车。本条目除本型外，也一并介绍同时期为适应保线作业现代化而制造的业务用货车101型、161型。

章节.155形:
伴随实施直通神户高速铁道，于1969年8月由武库川车辆工业制造的大型高性能救援车。常备于石屋川车库。
车体为全长18.7m、全宽2.76m的大型车体，涂成与先前登场的151型各型相同的红褐色。平头双驾驶台的车头设有2片正面窗，头部中央装2盏前照灯，左右装有标志灯。设有1.3m宽的大型平开门、平台及动力尾板，使重物装卸成为可能。侧面设有2处无窗的2m宽双开门，侧窗为推拉式铝制窗框窗，单侧4处。无窗部分设有架子、挂钩等，以搭载救援用资材。
转向架及电气设备为3011型的流用品，搭载3561型3568在设备换装时产生的东芝制设备，转向架装用TT-6，电动机搭载4台输出60kW的SE-516，控制器装备PE-15C-H。虽未设置车钩，但为可设置的结构。
章节.101形: 1962年由武库川车辆工业制造的钢轨运输车。外观与仅在转向架上安装钢轨吊装用链滑车和连接杆的轨道平车等十分相似。平时留置在今津站附近的侧线上，出动时与151型各型连结并被牵引。为此，车钩装有与151型简易车钩的承座相对应的销链式简易型车钩，制动装置则搭载了自动直通制动的AMM。
章节.161形: 用于碎石运输、于1965年12月由日立制作所制造的漏斗车。装载荷重25t，与国铁同系车ホキ800型形态相同，涂色也同样为纯黑色，但安装了万隆式密着车钩以及电车样式的尾灯，是私铁自有车辆的特征。与101型一样平时留置在今津站附近的侧线上，出动时由轨道机动车牵引。不过，它也可与151型各型连结，留下了与154连结的照片。1988年12月报废。
章节.变迁:
155型登场时所设想的事态所幸并未发生，除在工厂进出场时往返于石屋川车库与尼崎车库之间外，没有其他移动的机会。101型和161型曾出动进行保线工程，但因是夜间出动，很少能看到其白天活动的身姿。1971年将101所搭载的手动链滑车换装为电动葫芦。
随着时代变化，将工程用货车按机械处理的事业者不断增加。阪神也不例外，1982年101被新型钢轨运输车替换而报废，1988年161被自卸式轨道车替代而报废。替代车均为保线用、按机械处理且无车籍。
此后155的受电弓被更换为下框交叉式，在旧型救援车153的替代车110登场后，仍继续在石屋川车库待命，但实际上，若地下线内发生事故，电车难以靠近，于是改为用汽车出动，在事故现场附近的车站搬入资材进行复旧作业的方法。因此成为多余的155于1992年7月24日办理报废。

英文.首段: The Hanshin 155 series (はんしん155がたでんしゃ) was a railway vehicle formerly owned by Hanshin Electric Railway, a departmental electric freight car combining a newly built body with diverted bogies and electrical equipment. In addition to this type, this article also introduces the 101 and 161 series departmental freight cars built around the same time in response to the modernization of track maintenance work.

章节.155 series:
A large, high-performance rescue car built in August 1969 by Mukogawa Sharyo Kogyo in connection with the start of through services onto Kobe Rapid Transit Railway. It was kept on standby at Ishiyagawa Depot.
The body is a large body 18.7 m long and 2.76 m wide, painted the same reddish-brown as the previously introduced 151 series types. The front of the double-ended cab with flat ends had two front windows, two headlights at the center of the upper part, and marker lights on the left and right. A large 1.3 m wide hinged door, a platform, and a power gate were provided to enable loading and unloading of heavy objects. On the sides there were two 2 m wide windowless double doors, and side windows were sliding aluminum sash windows, four per side. Shelves and hooks were provided in the windowless parts to carry rescue materials.
The bogies and electrical equipment were diverted from the 3011 series, mounting Toshiba-made equipment that arose when the equipment of 3561 series 3568 was replaced; the bogies were TT-6, the motors were four SE-516 rated at 60 kW, and the controller was a PE-15C-H. No coupler was fitted, but the structure allowed one to be installed.
章节.101 series: A rail carrier built in 1962 by Mukogawa Sharyo Kogyo. Its appearance is very similar to a flatcar on which only a chain block for lifting rails and a connecting bar are mounted on a bogie. It was normally stabled on a siding near Imazu Station, and when dispatched it was coupled to and towed by the 151 series types. For this reason, in addition to a pin-link type simplified coupler compatible with the simplified coupler socket of the 151 series, it was fitted with an AMM automatic straight air brake as its braking device.
章节.161 series: A hopper car built by Hitachi in December 1965 for transporting crushed stone. Its payload is 25 t, and it has the same form as the JNR equivalent Hoki 800 type with the same all-black livery, but the features characteristic of a privately owned car are that it is fitted with a Bandon-type tight-lock coupler and electric-car-style tail lights. Like the 101 series, it was normally stabled on a siding near Imazu Station, and when dispatched it was towed by a motor car. However, it could be coupled to the 151 series types as well, and a photograph of it coupled to 154 survives. Scrapped in December 1988.
章节.Changes:
Fortunately, the kind of situation envisioned when the 155 series appeared did not occur, and apart from shuttling between Ishiyagawa Depot and Amagasaki Depot when entering and leaving the works, it had no opportunity to move. The 101 and 161 series were dispatched for track maintenance work, but because they were dispatched at night, it was rare to see them moving in the daytime. In 1971, the manual chain block carried by 101 was replaced with an electric hoist.
As times changed, more and more operators treated construction freight cars as machinery. Hanshin was no exception: in 1982, 101 was replaced by a new rail carrier and scrapped, and in 1988, 161 was replaced by a dump trolley and scrapped. Both replacement cars are treated as machinery for track maintenance and have no vehicle registration.
Later, the pantograph of 155 was replaced with a lower-frame crossed type, and even after the appearance of 110, the replacement for the older rescue car 153, it continued to stand by at Ishiyagawa Depot; however, in practice, because it is difficult for an electric car to approach an accident inside an underground line, the method came to be adopted of dispatching by automobile, carrying materials into a station near the accident site, and carrying out recovery work. Because of this, 155 became surplus and was scrapped as of July 24, 1992.

The body is a large body 18.7 m long and 2.76 m wide, painted the same reddish-brown as the previously introduced 151 series types. The front of the double-ended cab with flat ends had two front windows, two headlights at the center of the upper part, and marker lights on the left and right. A large 1.3 m wide hinged door, a platform, and a power gate were provided to enable loading and unloading of heavy objects. On the sides there were two 2 m wide windowless double doors, and side windows were sliding aluminum sash windows, four per side. Shelves and hooks were provided in the windowless parts to carry rescue materials.
The bogies and electrical equipment were diverted from the 3011 series, mounting Toshiba-made equipment that arose when the equipment of 3561 series 3568 was replaced; the bogies were TT-6, the motors were four SE-516 rated at 60 kW, and the controller was a PE-15C-H. No coupler was fitted, but the structure allowed one to be installed.

=== 101 series ===
A rail carrier built in 1962 by Mukogawa Sharyo Kogyo. Its appearance is very similar to a flatcar on which only a chain block for lifting rails and a connecting bar are mounted on a bogie. It was normally stabled on a siding near Imazu Station, and when dispatched it was coupled to and towed by the 151 series types. For this reason, in addition to a pin-link type simplified coupler compatible with the simplified coupler socket of the 151 series, it was fitted with an AMM automatic straight air brake as its braking device.

=== 161 series ===
A hopper car built by Hitachi in December 1965 for transporting crushed stone. Its payload is 25 t, and it has the same form as the JNR equivalent Hoki 800 type with the same all-black livery, but the features characteristic of a privately owned car are that it is fitted with a Bandon-type tight-lock coupler and electric-car-style tail lights. Like the 101 series, it was normally stabled on a siding near Imazu Station, and when dispatched it was towed by a motor car. However, it could be coupled to the 151 series types as well, and a photograph of it coupled to 154 survives. Scrapped in December 1988.

== Changes ==
Fortunately, the kind of situation envisioned when the 155 series appeared did not occur, and apart from shuttling between Ishiyagawa Depot and Amagasaki Depot when entering and leaving the works, it had no opportunity to move. The 101 and 161 series were dispatched for track maintenance work, but because they were dispatched at night, it was rare to see them moving in the daytime. In 1971, the manual chain block carried by 101 was replaced with an electric hoist.
As times changed, more and more operators treated construction freight cars as machinery. Hanshin was no exception: in 1982, 101 was replaced by a new rail carrier and scrapped, and in 1988, 161 was replaced by a dump trolley and scrapped. Both replacement cars are treated as machinery for track maintenance and have no vehicle registration.
Later, the pantograph of 155 was replaced with a lower-frame crossed type, and even after the appearance of 110, the replacement for the older rescue car 153, it continued to stand by at Ishiyagawa Depot; however, in practice, because it is difficult for an electric car to approach an accident inside an underground line, the method came to be adopted of dispatching by automobile, carrying materials into a station near the accident site, and carrying out recovery work. Because of this, 155 became surplus and was scrapped as of July 24, 1992.
